props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: The ids of the elements that describe the number input.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The number input's name when there is no `label`. It names the field box too.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The ids of the elements that name the number input, in place of `label`.

props.name: aria-required
props.description: Whether screen readers announce the number input as required. It does not validate, so an empty field still submits. Use `isRequired` for the browser's constraint check, and this for a rule a schema can relax.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: The number input's `autoComplete`, also passed to the country picker.

props.name: autoDetectCountry
props.description: Whether the field picks the country from a `+` or `00` prefix as the user types or pastes. Pass `false` to keep the selected country.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Whether the number input takes focus when the field mounts.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes for the field's root.

props.name: container
props.description: Where the country popup renders. It defaults to the nearest `ThemeScope` element.

props.name: countries
props.description: The countries the picker offers, as ISO codes. Defaults to every country. The metadata still parses every number. Detection only selects a listed country, so a number from another one stays in international form beside the selected country, as with trimmed metadata. With one country, the field shows its flag and dial code as plain text instead of a picker. The field ignores codes outside the catalog, without a packaged flag or in the product exclusions, and a list that leaves no country throws. A change that drops the selected country keeps the shown number's international identity, except a controlled `raw` value, which names no country and is read again in the country that remains. The rows sort by name whatever the list's order.

props.name: countryCode
props.description: The country, for a controlled country. Pass it with `onCountryChange`, in place of `defaultCountryCode`. Leave it out for an uncontrolled country. The field shows the country a controlled `value` names with its own `+` or `00` prefix while `autoDetectCountry` is on, else the country of a proposal the parent holds, else `countryCode`. It reads a value without a prefix, or an uncontrolled `defaultValue`, in `countryCode`. A new `countryCode`, or a `countries` or `metadata` change that resolves it to another country, acts like a pick. It clears the digits unless `preserveOnCountryChange` keeps them, and proposes the result through `onChange`. A change that leaves the country in place keeps the number. A pick, or a country detected while typing or pasting, is a proposal. The field shows it once the parent sets `countryCode` to it, and a parent that keeps its code returns the field to it. An uncontrolled number reports a pick's number only once the field shows it, so a rejected pick reports nothing. Each proposal reaches `onChange` at most once, whatever order the parent answers in. `onChange` describes when a call is replaced, canceled or skipped, as inside a hidden `<Activity>`. A proposal the parent has not answered yet keeps waiting through a render with the same props, and through a change to `defaultValue`, `defaultCountryCode` or `preserveOnCountryChange` alone. It also waits through a change to `outputFormat`, `international`, `formatOnType`, `autoDetectCountry`, `metadata` or `countries` that keeps `value` and `countryCode`, while `countries` still offers the proposal's country. An answer to one half of it keeps it waiting for the other, in either order: `countryCode` set to its country, or a `value` that is its number in a countryless form of the parent's own, such as national digits. A code that only falls back to the proposal's country is no answer. A proposal answered in full ends, as does one whose number the parent holds while the value names another country. Any other change drops it. A code the picker does not offer resolves as `defaultCountryCode` does. Removing `countryCode` keeps the country and number the field shows.

props.name: defaultCountryCode
props.description: The starting country. It must be a libphonenumber country with a packaged flag. A code the picker does not offer, because it is outside `countries`, excluded or untyped, falls back to `NO` when the picker offers it, else to the first offered country in catalog order. The field ignores it while `countryCode` is set.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The starting number of an uncontrolled field, read on mount as `value` is. A native form reset restores it, reads it again under the current props, and calls `onCountryChange` when that changes the country. `""` restores an empty number in `defaultCountryCode`. Without a `defaultValue`, a reset clears the digits and keeps the country. A later change leaves the shown number alone and becomes the next reset's target. The field ignores it while `value` is set, even to `""`.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting text, rendered as `Field.Description`.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content at the end of the field box, such as a button that acts on the number.

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description: The number input's `enterKeyHint`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: The error message, rendered as `Field.Error` while it is truthy. Pass `isInvalid` with it, so the field is marked invalid too. Without it, the field shows a `Form` error under `name`, or the number input's constraint message.

props.name: formatOnType
props.description: Whether the field formats the display as the user types. A national entry keeps the trunk prefix it was typed with, so a Swedish "0701234567" shows "070-123 45 67", and one typed without it stays ungrouped. A number detected from a `+` or `00` prefix shows in the national format.

props.name: id
props.description: The number input's `id`.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: The number input's `inputMode`, which picks the on-screen keyboard.

props.name: international
props.description: Whether the display keeps the typed digits and international prefixes. An accepted national draft stays national.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the field is disabled: editing, the country picker, and both the visible and the hidden input.

props.name: isInvalid
props.description: Whether the field is invalid, with the invalid look on the field box.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Whether the field blocks edits, paste and country changes. The field stays focusable and still submits, with the muted read-only fill.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the number input is required, so the browser's constraint check blocks an empty submit.

props.name: label
props.description: The visible label, rendered as `Field.Label`. Without it, name the field with `aria-label`.

props.name: metadata
props.description: Custom or trimmed libphonenumber metadata. A new metadata object updates the picker and reads the number shown again. Under a controlled `countryCode`, the new metadata reads a controlled `value` again as written, which may give the number another international identity. When the field shows a user's edit whose output equals `value`, such as a paste, it keeps that edit instead. While `countryCode` stays controlled and resolves to the same country, a render that releases `value` with the new metadata gives the same number as the new metadata in one render and the release in the next. For example, an FI-controlled field over `["FI", "SE"]` with raw output holds `+46701234567`, and `libphonenumber-js/metadata.max.json` replaces the default metadata. A render that still holds `value` submits `701234567`, and both paths through the release submit `+46701234567`. A shallow copy, such as `{ ...metadata }` written in a render, is the same metadata and replaces nothing. To limit the picker, pass `countries` instead, since trimmed metadata can no longer parse the numbers it leaves out. It does not make the bundle smaller, since the field imports its full default metadata either way.

props.name: name
props.description: The name the number submits under, from a hidden input. The visible input takes `${name}-display-value`. Without it, neither input submits. Inside a `Form`, the field shows the form's error under this name, removes it when the submitted number changes, and gives `onFormSubmit` the number under this name, in `outputFormat`.

props.name: noCountriesFoundText
props.description: Replaces the `noCountries` text of the locale dictionary, shown when no country matches.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Called when the number input loses focus.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with a proposed number in `outputFormat`. A controlled field shows it once the parent accepts it. The field calls it only when the proposal differs from the number the parent holds: `value`, compared exactly, or the output an uncontrolled field already shows. So deleting a separator, which keeps the number, calls nothing, while a parent that stores another form of the number, such as national digits, hears every proposal. While a country the user picked, pasted or typed waits for the parent and the picker still offers it, a new `countryCode` that accepts it or moves the field to another country makes an uncontrolled field compare with the output from before that proposal, even if the shown output changed during the wait. Inside a hidden `<Activity>`, a props change that would call it, such as a new `countryCode`, queues the call until the field shows again. An uncontrolled field then sends the number it submits, and nothing when that number is the output from before the proposal. A controlled field sends the number the change proposed. A later change that would call it replaces the queued call, so `countryCode` moved from `NO` to `SE` to `DK` while hidden, with `outputFormat="e164"` and `preserveOnCountryChange`, sends only `+4541234567` for `41234567`. A new `value` cancels a call queued before it. It is also called once as hydration commits, with a number typed or autofilled before the client scripts ran, under the same rule. A controlled parent accepts or rejects it like any other proposal.

props.name: onCountryChange
props.description: Called when the selected country changes. With `countryCode` set, it is called instead once as each disagreement starts, with the country of a proposal waiting for the parent, else the one shown, when it differs from `countryCode`. When `value` is set and the field already shows the proposed number in the proposal's country as the user makes the proposal, it is called with the shown country instead. A proposal the field first shows in its country after a later render does not count, such as a pick made with `autoDetectCountry` off whose kept digits show its country once detection turns on. It never hears the code the parent just set. A proposal that moves the country calls it before `onChange`, so a parent that takes both at once reads the number in the new country.

props.name: outputFormat
props.description: The format `onChange` reports and the hidden input submits.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The number input's placeholder text.

props.name: preserveOnCountryChange
props.description: Whether the digits stay when the country changes. Otherwise a country change clears them, and calls `onChange` with `""` unless the parent already holds `""`.

props.name: searchCountriesLabel
props.description: Replaces the `searchCountries` text of the locale dictionary, the country search box's name.

props.name: selectCountryLabel
props.description: Replaces the `selectCountry` text of the locale dictionary: the country popup's name and the country button's description. The button's name is its visible dial code and the selected country, such as "+47 Norway".

props.name: size
props.description: The control size of the field box around the country picker and the number, also written as `data-size`. `default` is the md control size, and `sm` the sm one. The search box in the country popup keeps the default size.

props.name: value
props.description: The number, for a controlled field. The field decodes it as a URI component when it arrives. Leave it out for an uncontrolled field.
